2	
3	Framework: Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules; three.js 0.185.1 is also installed for procedural asset factories, see BRIDGE.md).

5	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, drawing into the existing canvas with id #app. Show a glossy, candy-red, car-paint finished object on a slowly rotating turntable in a dark showroom. Since no model files are provided, construct the object procedurally from smooth shapes, for example a rounded, streamlined capsule or bean body with a separate smooth cabin bump and four dark rubber wheel discs, or any other smooth body with clearly curved, large reflective panels. The paint must look like automotive paint: a deep coloured base layer with fine metallic flake sparkle, topped by a glossy clear coat that mirrors a studio environment (long soft-box strip reflections that bend over the curved panels). Add chrome trim, such as a thin ring or strip, and a dark glass or black cabin panel for contrast. The turntable is a circular platform with a subtle ring light or reflective floor on which the object is mirrored faintly. Use a dark background with two or three long strip lights above and to the sides, plus a faint cool rim light, so the reflections read as soft-box highlights. 1	# three.js asset bridge (`aura3d import-three`)
2	
3	Carry procedural three.js content into an Aura3D project as a typed asset plus editable Aura3D source, instead of
4	porting it by hand. The bridge carries assets, animation clips, simple shaders, lights, camera and renderer output.
5	Behaviour (input, physics, scoring, UI) stays native Aura3D code. It is a build-time tool: `three` is a dev
6	dependency of your project, never a runtime dependency, and the shipped route imports only `@aura3d/engine`.
7	
8	Status: prototype (B1). Every run writes a report of what was carried, approximated or left out; read it before
9	you show the result.
10	
11	## When to use it
12	
13	| You have | Use |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| A three.js function that builds a scene from code (procedural props, a generated city, an animated rig, a shader showcase) | `aura3d import-three` |

import { camera, createAuraApp, environments, interactions, lights, material, primitives, scene } from "@aura3d/engine";

// A product on a procedural pedestal: torus knot (clear-coated metal), cylinder plinth, round stage, neutral environment.
// Metals reflect the environment, so environments.neutral is what makes this read as metal instead of grey plastic.
const app = createAuraApp("#app", {
  scene: scene({ background: "#d9dde3" })
    .add(environments.neutral({ intensity: 1.15, background: false }))
    .add(lights.directional({ name: "key", position: [4, 6.5, 4.5], target: [0, 1, 0], intensity: 2.8, color: "#fff4e6", shadow: true }))

The app renders a candy-red car on a slowly rotating turntable in a dark showroom, and it typechecks and builds. I did not build the faint mirrored reflection of the car on the platform. The platform top is instead polished and picks up the studio highlights.

- **Scene content:** `recipes/carpaint.mjs` builds the car, imported with `import_three` into `src/three-bridge/carpaint.*` (the `.bridge.ts` file is generated; I did not touch `carpaint.scene.ts`, which `main.ts` doesn't use). The car has a smooth body, a dark glass cabin with a red roof, a chrome belt line and window trim, and four dark rubber wheels with chrome rims. The platform has a chrome edge, a glowing ring light and tick marks.
- **Paint:** the candy-red base has a fine flake normal map generated in code, under a clearcoat layer.
- **Lighting and camera (`src/main.ts`):** a studio "softbox" environment, three rect-area strip lights (two overhead, one at the side) and a faint cool rim light. The camera stays fixed at a low front-three-quarter angle with the whole object in frame.
- **Turntable:** the platform and car rotate at 20°/s. `window.__TASK_STATE__` is updated every frame with the increasing `turntableAngleDeg` and `paintFinish: 'clearcoat'`. `window.__EVAL_READY__` is set after the first frame.
- **Mirror:** a planar mirror on the platform only showed the car's dark underside as a black square, so I removed it.

The roof cap floats slightly above the glass in the last screenshot.
